question_text: Under the IFSCA (CMI) Regulations, 2025, the term "International Financial Services Centre (IFSC)" has the meaning assigned to it under which statute?
option_a: Clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the IFSCA Act, 2019
option_b: Section 2(q) of the SEZ Act, 2005
explanation: Regulation 2(1)(x) adopts the definition of IFSC from clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the IFSCA Act, 2019.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The International Financial Services Centres Authority Act was enacted in which year?
explanation: The IFSCA Act, 2019 (Act No. 50 of 2019) is the parent statute establishing IFSCA as the unified regulator for IFSCs in India.
regulatory_source: IFSCA AML/CFT/KYC Guidelines, 2022 (updated 26.02.2026)

question_text: A "Foreign Jurisdiction" under the CMI Regulations means a country other than India whose securities market regulator is:
option_a: A member of the Financial Action Task Force
option_b: A signatory to IOSCO's Multilateral MoU (Appendix A) or to a bilateral MoU with IFSCA
option_c: Recognised by SEBI under the FPI Regulations
option_d: A member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision
explanation: Reg. 2(1)(u): the regulator must be an IOSCO MMoU Appendix A signatory or a signatory to a bilateral MoU with the Authority, and the country must not be adversely listed by FATF.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Which of the following countries would NOT qualify as a "Foreign Jurisdiction" under the CMI Regulations even if its regulator is an IOSCO MMoU signatory?
option_a: A country identified by FATF as having strategic AML/CFT deficiencies to which counter measures apply
option_b: A country that has signed a bilateral MoU with IFSCA
option_c: A country whose currency is not freely convertible
option_d: A country that is not a member of the United Nations
explanation: Reg. 2(1)(u) expressly excludes jurisdictions on FATF public statements — those subject to counter measures or with insufficient progress on action plans.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The ICSI Certificate Course on Regulatory Framework for Capital Market Intermediaries in IFSC is accredited by:
option_b: RBI
explanation: The course is accredited by IFSCA vide circular F. No. IFSCA-PLNP/80/2024-Capital Markets dated April 2, 2026.
regulatory_source: ICSI Course Brochure — Certificate Course on Regulatory Framework for CMIs in IFSC

question_text: Under the official ICSI assessment pattern for the CMI certificate course, the minimum qualifying marks are:
explanation: The assessment is 100 MCQs of 1 mark each over 90 minutes with no negative marking; the passing criterion is a minimum of 50% marks.
regulatory_source: ICSI Course Brochure — Certificate Course on Regulatory Framework for CMIs in IFSC

question_text: How many categories of activities require a certificate of registration as a CMI under Regulation 4(1) of the CMI Regulations, 2025?
explanation: Reg. 4(1) lists eleven registrable categories: broker dealer, clearing member, credit rating agency, custodian, debenture trustee, depository participant, distributor, ERDPP, investment adviser, investment banker and research entity.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under the 2026 amendment to the CMI Regulations, a unit in IFSC desirous of undertaking multiple activities may obtain:
option_b: A unified registration for such multiple activities
option_c: A deemed registration from the stock exchange
explanation: A proviso inserted w.e.f. 12.01.2026 permits a unified registration for multiple activities in the manner specified by the Authority.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A CMI seeking registration with IFSCA must be present in the IFSC in the form of:
option_a: Only a company incorporated in India
option_b: A company, an LLP, a body corporate, or a branch thereof
option_c: Only a wholly-owned subsidiary of a regulated entity
option_d: A partnership firm or sole proprietorship
explanation: Reg. 6 permits presence as a company, LLP, body corporate, or a branch of any of these.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Where a CMI is set up as a branch, its minimum net worth may be maintained at the parent level, provided that:
option_a: The parent is a listed entity
option_b: The net worth maintained at parent level is earmarked for the IFSC branch
option_c: The parent gives a bank guarantee to IFSCA
option_d: The branch remits profits to the parent annually
explanation: Reg. 7(2) proviso requires the minimum net worth maintained at the parent level to be earmarked for its branch in IFSC.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An entity operating as a CMI in multiple categories under the Regulations must maintain:
option_a: The sum of all applicable minimum net worth requirements
option_b: The average of applicable net worth requirements
option_c: The highest of the applicable minimum net worth requirements, unless otherwise specified
option_d: Only the net worth applicable to its principal activity
explanation: Reg. 7(4): the highest applicable minimum net worth applies for multi-category operations, unless the Authority specifies otherwise.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: For a broker dealer, clearing member or investment banker, "net worth" under the CMI Regulations means:
option_b: The aggregate value of its liquid assets
option_d: Tier-I capital as per Basel III
explanation: The proviso to Reg. 2(1)(cc) substitutes the general definition: for these three categories net worth means the aggregate value of liquid assets (cash, bank balance, fixed deposits, Government Securities and specified instruments).
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Which one of the following is a disqualification under the "fit and proper" criteria in Regulation 8?
option_a: The person has changed employment thrice in five years
option_b: The person has been declared a fugitive economic offender
option_c: The person holds directorships in more than two companies
option_d: The person is above 70 years of age
explanation: Reg. 8(2)(b)(xi) lists declaration as a fugitive economic offender among disqualifications, along with conviction for economic offences, insolvency, debarment orders in force, wilful default, etc.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A regulatory authority passed an order against Mr. X having a material bearing on the securities market. Two years have elapsed since the order. Under Regulation 8, Mr. X is:
option_a: Fit and proper, since the order was not a conviction
option_b: Not fit and proper, since three years from the date of such order have not elapsed
option_c: Fit and proper if he furnishes an indemnity bond
option_d: Automatically fit and proper on appeal being filed
explanation: Reg. 8(2)(b)(viii): a material order by the Authority or another regulator disqualifies the person until three years from the date of the order have elapsed; materiality is determined by the Authority.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The minimum experience requirement for a Principal Officer of a CMI is:
option_b: Three years in the financial services market
option_c: Five years in the securities market
explanation: Reg. 9(3)(a) requires at least three years' experience in the financial services market; for an ERDPP's PO, one year in ESG-related activities also suffices.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Following the 2026 amendment, the SAME person may act as principal officer for which combination of registrations of an entity?
option_a: Broker dealer, clearing member and depository participant only
option_b: Broker dealer, clearing member, depository participant, investment adviser, research entity, custodian and registered distributor
option_d: Investment banker and debenture trustee only
explanation: The substituted proviso to Reg. 9(8) (w.e.f. 12.01.2026) expanded the shared-PO list from three categories to seven; a separate vertical head is required for distribution activities, and CRA + ERDPP may also share a PO.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: If IFSCA finds deficiencies in a registration application, the applicant is given how much time to rectify them?
option_b: 30 days
explanation: Reg. 12(2): deficiencies are communicated giving thirty days' time; refusal follows only after an opportunity to make written submissions.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The certificate of registration granted to a CMI is valid for:
option_b: Three years
option_d: Perpetuity, unless suspended or cancelled by the Authority
explanation: Reg. 13 makes CMI registration perpetual unless suspended or cancelled — a frequent misconception is that it requires periodic renewal.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The annual compliance audit report of a CMI for a financial year must be furnished to the Authority by:
option_b: 30th June
explanation: Reg. 25(2): the compliance audit report must reach the Authority by 30th September; trading members, clearing members and DPs also file a copy with their respective MII.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The net worth requirement for a broker dealer (trading member) under Schedule I of the CMI Regulations is:
option_b: USD 1 million
option_c: As specified by the recognised stock exchange
explanation: Schedule I entrusts the broker dealer net worth to the recognised stock exchange, unlike categories with fixed USD amounts.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An application for registration as a broker dealer is made:
option_a: Directly to IFSCA in physical form
option_b: Through SWIT along with additional information routed through the recognised stock exchange
explanation: Reg. 5(1) proviso: broker dealer, clearing member and DP applications are made through the respective market infrastructure institution, which examines eligibility and forwards with recommendation.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The recognised stock exchange must forward a complete broker-dealer application to the Authority with its recommendation within:
option_b: 15 days
explanation: Reg. 5(2): the MII must examine eligibility and forward the application no later than thirty days of receipt of the complete application.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A broker dealer wishes to also act as a clearing member in a recognised clearing corporation. Under Regulation 5(5), it:
option_a: Must obtain a fresh certificate of registration from IFSCA
option_b: May do so subject to approval of the concerned clearing corporation, without a separate certificate of registration
explanation: Reg. 5(5)(a): with the clearing corporation's approval, a broker dealer may act as clearing member without any separate registration certificate; the mirror rule in 5(4)(a) lets a clearing member act as broker dealer.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under the Code of Conduct, a broker dealer shall NOT:
option_b: Encourage sales or purchases of securities with the sole object of generating brokerage
option_c: Operate on more than one recognised stock exchange
option_d: Execute orders at the best available price
explanation: Schedule II Part B(A) para 7 prohibits churning-style dealing aimed solely at generating brokerage or commission; para 4 in fact obliges dealing with small investors and best-price execution.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A broker dealer must issue to its client, without delay, for all transactions:
option_b: A contract note in the form specified by the recognised stock exchange
explanation: Schedule II Part B(A) para 6 mandates prompt issue of contract notes in the exchange-specified form.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Which statement about a broker dealer's conduct is CORRECT under the Code of Conduct?
option_a: It may furnish optimistic quotations to induce business if disclosed later
option_b: It may refuse small investors on grounds of low volume
option_c: It shall not knowingly execute an order for a client who has failed to carry out commitments with another broker dealer
option_d: It may engage in speculative business without limit if margins are paid
explanation: Para 9 of Part B(A) bars dealing for defaulting clients of other broker dealers; paras 3, 4 and 8 prohibit excessive speculation, refusal of small investors, and misleading quotations respectively.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A broker dealer in IFSC must ensure compliance with:
option_b: Applicable laws including bye-laws, rules and regulations specified by the recognised stock exchange
option_d: The bye-laws of any foreign exchange where its parent operates
explanation: Reg. 26(1) obliges broker dealers to comply with the recognised stock exchange's bye-laws, rules and regulations in addition to applicable laws.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A broker dealer incorporated in IFSC undergoes an indirect change in control. Under Regulation 23, it must:
option_a: Intimate IFSCA within 15 days of the change
option_b: Seek prior approval of IFSCA
option_c: Merely notify the stock exchange after the change
option_d: Do nothing, as indirect changes are not covered
explanation: Reg. 23(2): a CMI incorporated in IFSC needs PRIOR approval for any direct or indirect change in control; only a branch operates on 15-day post-facto intimation under Reg. 23(1). The incorporated/branch distinction is a classic examination trap.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The net worth requirement for a clearing member under Schedule I is:
option_b: As specified by the recognised clearing corporation
option_d: As specified by the recognised stock exchange
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 2 leaves the clearing member net worth to the recognised clearing corporation.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A clearing member's application for registration is routed through:
option_b: The recognised stock exchange
explanation: Reg. 5(1) proviso routes clearing member applications through the recognised clearing corporation, which examines eligibility and forwards with recommendation within 30 days.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Subject to approval by the concerned clearing corporation, a clearing member may:
option_a: Operate in more than one recognised clearing corporation without a separate registration certificate
option_b: Act as a credit rating agency
option_d: Waive margin requirements for group entities
explanation: Reg. 5(5)(b) permits multi-CC operation with the concerned CC's approval, without any separate certificate of registration.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under Regulation 26(2), a clearing member shall ensure compliance with the bye-laws, rules and regulations specified by:
option_b: The recognised clearing corporation
explanation: Reg. 26(2) parallels the broker-dealer rule: a clearing member follows the recognised clearing corporation's framework.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A clearing member wishing to surrender its registration must file the application:
option_b: Through the recognised clearing corporation, and surrender is effective only on acceptance by the Authority
explanation: Reg. 14 proviso: trading member/clearing member/DP surrender applications go through the respective MII; the Explanation makes voluntary surrender effective only upon the Authority's acceptance.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: In addition to filing its annual compliance audit report with the Authority, a clearing member must file a copy with:
option_b: The recognised clearing corporation
explanation: Proviso to Reg. 25(2): trading members file with the exchange, clearing members with the clearing corporation, and DPs with the depository.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An IFSC branch of a foreign bank acting as clearing member experiences a change in control of its parent. Under Regulation 23 it must:
option_b: Intimate the Authority and the market infrastructure institution of which it is a member within fifteen days
explanation: Reg. 23(1): a CMI operating as a BRANCH intimates the Authority and its MII within 15 days of any direct or indirect change in control — prior approval applies only to IFSC-incorporated CMIs.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The net worth requirement for a Debenture Trustee under Schedule I is:
option_b: USD 1.5 million
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 5 fixes the debenture trustee net worth at USD 1.5 million — the highest fixed amount in the Schedule.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A registered debenture trustee shall enter into an agreement with the issuer:
option_b: Before the opening of the subscription list for the issue of debentures
option_d: Only if the issue exceeds USD 50 million
explanation: Reg. 30(1) requires the trustee-issuer agreement before the subscription list opens.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A person shall NOT be appointed as debenture trustee where:
option_a: It is an associate of the issuer or is likely to have a conflict of interest
option_b: It is registered with a foreign regulator
option_c: It has previously acted as trustee for the same issuer
option_d: Its net worth exceeds USD 5 million
explanation: Reg. 30(2) bars appointment where the trustee is an associate of the issuer or is likely to have any conflict of interest.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A debenture trustee must call for periodical/performance reports from the issuer within:
option_a: Seven days of the relevant board meeting or forty-five days of the respective quarter, whichever is earlier
option_b: Thirty days of each quarter end
option_d: Ninety days of the financial year end
explanation: Reg. 30(3)(c) fixes the dual timeline: 7 days from the relevant board meeting or 45 days from the quarter, whichever is earlier.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A debenture trustee must appoint a nominee director on the board of the issuer in the event of:
option_b: Two consecutive defaults in payment of interest, or default in creation of security, or default in redemption of debentures
option_c: A fall in the issuer's credit rating
option_d: A request by 10% of debenture holders
explanation: Reg. 30(3)(f) triggers nominee director appointment on two consecutive interest defaults, or default in security creation, or default in redemption; the issuer must provide requisite support where legally permissible.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: On becoming aware of a breach of the trust deed or of any applicable law, the debenture trustee shall inform the Authority:
option_b: Within 45 days
option_d: Only if debenture holders so resolve
explanation: Reg. 30(3)(q) requires the trustee to inform the Authority immediately of any breach of the trust deed or provision of applicable laws.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Which statement regarding relinquishment by a debenture trustee is correct?
option_a: It may relinquish on 30 days' notice to the issuer
option_b: It shall not relinquish its assignment unless and until another debenture trustee is appointed in its place by the issuer
option_c: It may relinquish with the consent of 51% of debenture holders
explanation: Reg. 30(5) prohibits relinquishment until a replacement trustee is appointed by the issuer, ensuring debenture holders are never left unprotected.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under section 71(5) of the Companies Act, 2013, appointment of a debenture trustee is mandatory before a company issues a prospectus or makes an offer of debentures to the public or to its members exceeding:
option_b: Two hundred persons
explanation: Section 71(5) requires debenture trustee appointment before any prospectus or offer/invitation to the public or to members exceeding five hundred.
regulatory_source: Companies Act, 2013 (as amended up to 01.04.2021)

question_text: A trust deed contains a clause fully exempting the debenture trustee from liability for breach of trust even where it fails to exercise due care. Under section 71(7) of the Companies Act, 2013, this clause is:
option_a: Valid if disclosed in the prospectus
option_b: Void, though liability may be subject to exemptions agreed by a majority of debenture holders holding not less than three-fourths in value at a meeting
option_d: Voidable at the option of the issuer
explanation: Section 71(7) voids blanket indemnity/exemption clauses; only debenture holders holding not less than 3/4ths in value, at a meeting, may agree to exemptions.
regulatory_source: Companies Act, 2013 (as amended up to 01.04.2021)

question_text: The net worth requirement for an Investment Banker under Schedule I is:
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 10 fixes the investment banker net worth at USD 100,000 — measured as liquid assets per the proviso to Reg. 2(1)(cc).
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: "Investment banker" under the CMI Regulations means a person in the business of:
option_b: Issue management, including arrangements for selling, buying or subscribing to securities, or acting as manager, consultant or adviser to such issue management
explanation: Reg. 2(1)(aa) defines an investment banker around issue management and related corporate advisory services.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A Banking Unit in IFSC may act as an investment banker:
option_b: Subject to authorisation in accordance with the requirements specified by the Authority
explanation: Reg. 4(3) permits a Banking Unit to act as investment banker subject to authorisation; Reg. 4(2) separately lets it act as banker to an issue.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An investment banker shall enter into an agreement with the issuer specifying:
option_a: The dividend policy of the issuer
option_b: The roles and responsibilities of the investment banker in the issue
option_c: The listing venue of the promoter group
option_d: The credit rating to be obtained
explanation: Reg. 35(1) mandates an issue-management agreement setting out the banker's roles and responsibilities.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Where there is more than one lead investment banker to an issue:
option_a: Only the first-appointed banker is responsible
option_b: The responsibilities of each lead investment banker shall be clearly demarcated
option_c: Liability is automatically joint and several for all functions
explanation: Reg. 35(2) requires clear demarcation of responsibilities among multiple lead investment bankers.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: If the investment banker is a promoter or an associate of the issuer, it shall not undertake any activity in the issue EXCEPT:
option_b: Pricing of the issue
option_c: Marketing of the issue or offer
explanation: Reg. 35(3) restricts a promoter/associate investment banker to marketing of the issue or offer only.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An IFSC entity holds registrations as investment banker and debenture trustee. For net worth purposes it must maintain:
option_b: USD 1.5 million, being the highest of the applicable requirements
option_c: USD 1.6 million, being the sum of both
explanation: Reg. 7(4): multi-category CMIs maintain the highest applicable minimum net worth — here USD 1.5 million (debenture trustee) exceeds USD 100,000 (investment banker).
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Following the January 2026 amendment, the net worth requirement for a Custodian under Schedule I is:
option_a: As specified by the Authority from time to time
option_b: USD 1 million
explanation: The 2026 amendment substituted the earlier "as specified by the Authority" entry with a fixed USD 1 million requirement.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Custodians already registered with the Authority that need to infuse or earmark additional funds under the revised net worth norms must comply by:
option_b: January 12, 2026
explanation: The Schedule I note (inserted 12.01.2026) gives existing custodians until June 30, 2026 to meet the revised USD 1 million norm.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A custodian shall enter into an agreement with each client detailing:
option_b: Various circumstances relating to custody of the securities or other permitted financial products or funds
explanation: Reg. 29(3) mandates a client-wise custody agreement covering the circumstances of custody of securities, permitted financial products or funds.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A custodian's internal controls must be adequate to:
option_a: Prevent any manipulation of records and documents and protect records from theft and natural hazard
option_b: Guarantee investment returns to clients
explanation: Reg. 29(4) requires internal controls against manipulation of records and for protection from theft and natural hazard.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A custodian shall have adequate mechanisms for:
option_a: Reviewing, monitoring and evaluating its controls, systems, procedures and safeguards
option_b: Setting benchmark indices
explanation: Reg. 29(2) requires ongoing review, monitoring and evaluation of the custodian's controls, systems, procedures and safeguards.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under the 2026 amendment, which earlier IFSCA circular relating to custodians stands superseded?
option_a: Circular on Distribution of Capital Market Products dated 21.12.2022
option_b: Circular titled "Recognition as Custodian of assets/securities" dated February 24, 2021
option_c: Circular on ESG Ratings Providers dated 30.10.2024
explanation: Reg. 47(2A), inserted w.e.f. 12.01.2026, superseded the February 24, 2021 custodian-recognition circular.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Following the 2026 amendment to Regulation 9(8), a custodian that is also a registered distributor and investment adviser may:
option_b: Have the same person as principal officer for these activities, with a separate vertical head for distribution
option_c: Appoint its compliance officer as principal officer for all three
explanation: The substituted proviso to Reg. 9(8) includes custodian, registered distributor and investment adviser among the seven categories that may share a PO; a separate vertical head is required for the distribution business.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A global bank's IFSC branch acts as custodian. Its parent maintains the USD 1 million net worth in its home jurisdiction. This is compliant only if:
option_a: The parent is rated investment grade
option_b: The net worth maintained at the parent level is earmarked for the IFSC branch
option_c: The branch obtains a comfort letter from its home regulator
option_d: It is never compliant; the branch must hold funds locally
explanation: Reg. 7(2) permits branch-form CMIs to maintain the minimum net worth at parent level provided it is earmarked for the IFSC branch.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The net worth requirement for an Investment Adviser under Schedule I is:
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 9 fixes the investment adviser net worth at USD 25,000.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Advice given through newspapers, magazines or any electronic/broadcasting medium widely available to the public:
option_b: Is NOT considered investment advice for the purposes of the Regulations
option_d: Requires prior approval of IFSCA per article
explanation: The proviso to Reg. 2(1)(y) carves out widely-available media commentary from the definition of investment advice.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An investment adviser shall not receive any consideration, in any form, in respect of the underlying products or securities advised, from:
option_b: Any person other than the client being advised
explanation: Reg. 34(4) confines the adviser's remuneration to the advised client alone, eliminating issuer-side commissions — the core of the fiduciary standard in Reg. 34(3).
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An investment adviser shall not enter into transactions on its OWN account contrary to its advice to clients for a period of:
option_b: 15 days from the advice, unless a revised assessment is given to the client at least 24 hours before the transaction
explanation: Reg. 34(6): 15-day contra-trade bar; the proviso allows earlier dealing where a revised assessment is communicated at least 24 hours in advance.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Which of the following is a required element of an investment adviser's risk profiling process under Regulation 34(8)?
option_a: Communicating the risk profile to the client after completion of risk assessment
option_b: Obtaining a credit report of the client
option_d: Executing all trades for the client
explanation: Reg. 34(8) requires obtaining necessary information, a process for assessing risk tolerance, communication of the risk profile to the client, and periodic updation.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The arm's-length requirement between advisory and distribution activities obliges an investment adviser to provide advisory services through:
option_a: A separately identifiable department or division, including separate manpower
option_b: A different legal entity in all cases
explanation: Reg. 34(11): advisory must run through a separately identifiable department/division with separate manpower; Reg. 34(10) additionally requires client-level segregation between advisory and distribution.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An investment adviser providing implementation services to advisory clients must ensure that:
option_a: Clients are obliged to use those services
option_b: Conflicts are disclosed and any implementation fee is under an agreement and disclosed transparently
explanation: Reg. 34(12)-(13): implementation services are permitted with conflict disclosure and transparent, agreement-based fees; the client is never obliged to avail them.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under Regulation 34(7), an investment adviser shall not, on its own account:
option_b: Knowingly sell securities or investment products to, or purchase them from, a client
option_d: Maintain a bank account in IFSC
explanation: Reg. 34(7) prohibits knowingly acting as counterparty to one's own client — a principal-trade conflict rule distinct from the 15-day contra-trade bar.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A fintech firm in IFSC advises clients for fees and also distributes funds of its group entity. A client complains he was advised into the group fund without disclosure. Which combination of provisions is engaged?
option_a: Reg. 34(2)(b) conflict disclosure, Reg. 34(3) fiduciary duty, and Reg. 34(10)-(11) segregation of advisory and distribution
option_b: Only the Advertisement Code
explanation: Advising into an associated product without disclosure breaches conflict-disclosure (34(2)(b)), fiduciary duty (34(3)) and the advisory/distribution segregation architecture (34(10)-(11)).
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The net worth requirement for a Distributor under Schedule I is:
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 7 fixes the distributor net worth at USD 50,000.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: For distributing products or services of a regulated financial entity to ALL types of clients, the distributor must ensure the products/services have been:
option_a: Rated by a credit rating agency
option_b: Authorised, vetted or approved for offering to all types of investors by the relevant regulatory or supervisory authority of that entity
option_c: Listed on a recognised stock exchange
explanation: Reg. 32(2): retail-wide distribution is permitted only where the product/service is authorised, vetted or approved for all investor types by the entity's home regulator.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: When dealing with clients OTHER than sophisticated investors, a registered distributor must:
option_b: Undertake due diligence of the products and assess suitability, seeking information on the client's financial status, investment experience and objectives
explanation: Code of Conduct Part B(F) para 2 requires product due diligence and suitability assessment for non-sophisticated clients; para 5 permits a risk-understanding declaration route for sophisticated investors.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under the distributor Code of Conduct, a registered distributor shall abstain from attracting clients through:
option_b: Offer of rebate, kickback, gifts, etc.
explanation: Para 13 of Part B(F) prohibits rebates, kickbacks and gifts as client-acquisition inducements; para 22 separately prohibits encouraging churning for remuneration.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: If requested by a client, a distributor shall disclose:
option_b: The amount of direct and indirect remuneration, its basis, and whether any relation exists between the distributor and the product/service provider
explanation: Para 8 of Part B(F) mandates on-request disclosure of direct/indirect remuneration, its basis, and any relationship with the offering entity.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under the Advertisement Code for Distributors, advertisements shall NOT contain:
option_b: Testimonials or any ranking based on any criteria
option_d: Product characteristics consistent with the placement memorandum
explanation: Para 27 of the Advertisement Code bars false, misleading or assumption-based statements, testimonials and rankings; paras 26-31 require accurate, fair, complete and timely advertisements.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A registered distributor that also carries out proprietary investments must:
option_b: Ensure clear segregation of proprietary investments from those carried out as part of distribution activities
option_d: Report proprietary trades to clients daily
explanation: Para 15 of Part B(F) requires clear segregation of proprietary and distribution-linked investments; omnibus structures, where allowed, must meet all applicable norms.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The December 21, 2022 IFSCA circular on Distribution of Capital Market Products under the 2021 Regulations is applied by a distributor after commencement of the 2025 Regulations. This is:
option_a: Correct, all old circulars survive indefinitely
option_b: Incorrect — that circular stands expressly superseded under Regulation 47(2)(a)
option_d: A matter of the distributor's discretion
explanation: Reg. 47(2)(a) expressly supersedes the 21.12.2022 distribution circular; distribution is now governed by Reg. 32 and Schedule II Part B(F).
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The net worth requirement for a Credit Rating Agency under Schedule I is:
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 3 fixes the CRA net worth at USD 200,000.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A registered CRA shall enter into a written agreement with each client which must include:
option_b: The rights and liabilities of each party and the fee to be charged
explanation: Reg. 28(1) mandates a written client agreement covering rights, liabilities and fees.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: After assigning a rating, a registered CRA shall:
option_a: Withdraw it after one year automatically
option_b: Continuously monitor the rating and carry out periodic reviews, unless the rating is withdrawn
option_c: Review it only on client request
option_d: Freeze it for the life of the instrument
explanation: Reg. 28(4) imposes continuous monitoring and periodic review obligations for outstanding ratings.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: As a general rule under Regulation 28(5), a CRA shall not withdraw a rating so long as:
option_a: The client has not paid renewal fees
option_b: The obligations under the rated security, instrument or facility are outstanding
explanation: Reg. 28(5): no withdrawal while obligations under the rated instrument are outstanding, subject to the specific situations in its proviso.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The CRA Code of Conduct requires a rating agency to maintain what kind of relationship between its credit rating activity and other activities?
option_b: An arm's length relationship
explanation: Schedule II Part B(B) para 2 requires an arm's-length relationship between the rating function and other business, alongside the para 1 duty of due diligence and independent professional judgment.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A CRA registered with IFSCA and also registered as an ERDPP may, under the provisos to Regulation 9(8):
option_b: Have the same person as principal officer for both activities
option_c: Share a principal officer only with a broker dealer
explanation: A specific proviso to Reg. 9(8) permits a common principal officer for CRA and ERDPP registrations of the same entity.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

topic_name: ESG Ratings and Data Products Providers in IFSC
question_text: The net worth requirement for an ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider under Schedule I is:
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 8 fixes the ERDPP net worth at USD 25,000.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

topic_name: ESG Ratings and Data Products Providers in IFSC
question_text: An ERDPP shall not provide any service other than ESG Ratings and ESG Data Products:
option_b: Without the prior approval of the Authority
option_d: Unless it converts into an LLP
explanation: Reg. 33(2): any other service requires the Authority's prior approval; Reg. 33(1) permits services in an IFSC or a Foreign Jurisdiction.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

topic_name: ESG Ratings and Data Products Providers in IFSC
question_text: The ERDPP Code of Conduct (good governance, quality systems, conflicts management, etc.) applies on what basis?
option_b: "Comply" or "explain" basis
explanation: Reg. 33(3) applies the principle-based ERDPP Code of Conduct on a comply-or-explain basis — unique among CMI categories.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

topic_name: ESG Ratings and Data Products Providers in IFSC
question_text: Under Regulation 33(7), an ERDPP shall segregate:
option_b: Its activities relating to ESG Ratings and ESG Data Products from its other activities, to avoid conflicts of interest
explanation: Reg. 33(7) requires segregation of the ESG Ratings/Data Products activities from other activities to prevent conflicts of interest.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The net worth requirement for a Research Entity under Schedule I is:
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 11 fixes the research entity net worth at USD 25,000.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Which of the following is EXEMPT from separate registration as a Research Entity when issuing or distributing research reports to the public?
option_a: A registered investment adviser, credit rating agency or Fund Management Entity
option_b: Any listed company
explanation: Reg. 4(4)(a) exempts IFSCA-registered investment advisers, CRAs and FMEs from separate research-entity registration for issuing/circulating research reports.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A research analyst may trade contrary to his own outstanding research recommendation:
option_a: Freely, as personal trades are unregulated
option_b: Never under any circumstances
option_c: Only in special circumstances with prior written approval for each trade
explanation: The research entity's policy must bar contra trading by analysts except in special circumstances with prior written approval per trade; remuneration must also be structured to avoid bias.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A research entity must disclose in its report, among other conflicts, beneficial ownership in the subject company of:
option_a: One or more per cent of its securities
option_b: Five or more per cent
explanation: The conflict-disclosure Explanation requires disclosure where the entity, analyst, associate or relative holds beneficial ownership of 1% or more of the subject company's securities, material financial interest, or a material business relationship in the past 12 months.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under Regulation 27, a CMI (including a broker dealer) desirous of dealing in securities in Foreign Jurisdictions shall:
option_a: Obtain a fresh registration in each foreign country
option_b: Comply with the norms and requirements specified by the Authority
option_c: Route all trades through SEBI-registered brokers
explanation: Reg. 27 is an enabling provision: global access is subject to norms and requirements to be specified by the Authority.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Until the norms under Regulation 27 of the 2025 Regulations are issued, dealing in securities in Foreign Jurisdictions continues to be governed by:
option_a: Chapter V of the IFSCA (CMI) Regulations, 2021, saved by the proviso to Regulation 47(1)
option_b: SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019
explanation: The proviso to Reg. 47(1) transitionally saves Chapter V of the repealed 2021 Regulations for global access until Reg. 27 norms are issued — a key example of a surviving provision of a repealed regulation.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: For global access purposes, the twin conditions in the "Foreign Jurisdiction" definition relate to:
option_b: IOSCO MMoU/bilateral MoU status of the securities regulator AND absence from adverse FATF public statements
option_d: Common law heritage and English language
explanation: Reg. 2(1)(u) combines a cooperation test (IOSCO MMoU Appendix A or bilateral MoU with IFSCA) with an AML integrity test (not FATF counter-measures/insufficient-progress listed).
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: An IFSC broker dealer began dealing in a Foreign Jurisdiction under the 2021 Regulations before their repeal. After the 2025 Regulations commenced, its prior registration and actions are:
option_b: Deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of the 2025 Regulations
option_d: Subject to fresh approval within 30 days
explanation: Reg. 47(3)(a): anything done, actions taken and registrations granted under the repealed regulations are deemed done under the corresponding provisions of the 2025 Regulations.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: The net worth requirement for a Depository Participant under Schedule I is:
option_d: As specified by the stock exchange
explanation: Schedule I, S. No. 6 leaves the DP net worth to the depository — like broker dealers (exchange) and clearing members (clearing corporation).
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A depository participant's application for registration is made through:
option_b: The recognised stock exchange
explanation: Reg. 5(1) proviso routes DP applications through the recognised depository, which examines eligibility and forwards with its recommendation within 30 days.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Under Regulation 31(2), a depository participant shall ensure that:
option_a: All beneficial owners share a single omnibus account
option_b: Separate accounts are opened in the name of each beneficial owner, and each owner's securities are segregated from other owners' and from the participant's own securities
option_c: Securities are pooled with the participant's own holdings for efficiency
option_d: Accounts are opened only for institutional investors
explanation: Reg. 31(2) mandates per-beneficial-owner accounts with strict segregation from other owners and from the DP's proprietary securities.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A depository participant shall ensure compliance with applicable laws including the bye-laws, rules and regulations specified by:
option_b: The recognised stock exchange
option_d: The Institute of Company Secretaries of India
explanation: Reg. 31(1) obliges DPs to comply with the recognised depository's framework.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: Which set of registrations may share a single principal officer with a depository participant registration under the amended Regulation 9(8)?
option_a: Broker dealer, clearing member, investment adviser, research entity, custodian and registered distributor
option_b: Debenture trustee and investment banker
option_d: None; a DP's PO must be exclusive
explanation: The substituted proviso to Reg. 9(8) groups seven categories — BD, CM, DP, IA, RE, custodian and registered distributor — as eligible to share one PO.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)

question_text: A depository participant wishes to voluntarily exit the IFSC. The correct surrender procedure is:
option_a: File directly with IFSCA; surrender is effective on filing
option_b: File through the recognised depository; the surrender is effective only after acceptance by the Authority
option_c: Simply close all client accounts and cease operations
option_d: Transfer registration to a group entity
explanation: Reg. 14: TM/CM/DP surrender applications are routed through the respective MII, and voluntary surrender takes effect only upon the Authority's acceptance.
regulatory_source: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12.01.2026)
